title: The 2017 SYSK Christmas Extravaganza!
summary: Annual SYSK Christmas special, ad-free by tradition. Hosts open with holiday banter and reflect on the year, then cover: whether the movie Die Hard is a Christmas movie (including an LA Weekly critic's argument and a quoted email from screenwriter Jeb Stewart about the original novel Nothing Lasts Forever by Roger Thorpe); the history of the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree, from its Depression-era origins by construction workers through its LED lights, Habitat for Humanity recycling, and star ornament; Christmas in space, from Apollo 8's 1968 broadcast to ISS holidays; twentieth-century must-have toys (Cabbage Patch Kids, Star Wars figures and vouchers, Tickle Me Elmo); and wassail, the warm boozy punch, with a beer-and-rum recipe. Closes with holiday wishes.
topics: Habitat for Humanity Christmas tree lumber

segments.title: Opening banter and holiday greetings
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the Christmas episode with banter, note that the Christmas and Halloween episodes stay ad-free, reflect on how fast the year went, and set up the segments.

segments.title: Is Die Hard a Christmas movie?
segments.summary: The hosts debate whether Die Hard is a Christmas movie. They discuss an LA Weekly piece by Art Tavana arguing it is, citing Holly and John McClane's names, the terrorist count, the Christmas miracle line, and the film's Christmas Eve setting. They then read an email from screenwriter Jeb Stewart, who says the story came from Roger Thorpe's novel Nothing Lasts Forever and that he made it a Christmas story on purpose.

segments.title: Rockefeller Center Christmas tree history
segments.summary: The hosts trace the Rockefeller Center tree from a twenty-foot tree bought by Depression-era construction workers, to the first official lighting, to radio and TV broadcasts. They cover tree selection, the LED switch, recycling through Habitat for Humanity, and the crystal star.

segments.title: Christmas in space
segments.summary: The hosts describe Apollo 8's 1968 Christmas Eve broadcast from lunar orbit, later Christmas aboard Skylab, the Space Shuttle mission, cosmonaut-era Christmas with John Blaha, and the International Space Station's Christmas mornings.

segments.title: Iconic twentieth-century Christmas toys
segments.summary: The hosts discuss must-have toys: Cabbage Patch Kids and their 1983 and 1984 craze, Star Wars action figures given out as vouchers in 1977, and Tickle Me Elmo's 1996 shortage, including reported stampedes.

segments.title: Wassail recipe
segments.summary: Chuck explains the etymology of wassail and the old tradition of wassailing. Josh gives a recipe for a beer and rum wassail with simple syrup, lemon, nutmeg, and ginger, and advises responsible drinking.

segments.title: Closing holiday wishes
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners, wish everyone happy holidays, and sign off.
